source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 2 · lesson 11. Exercises reused from the lesson; du'aas flagged for review.

learn.en: Fajr: from dawn until sunrise. Dhuhr: from just after midday until a shadow is as long as its object.
learn.title: Fajr and Dhuhr

learn.en: Asr: from then until just before sunset. Maghrib: right after sunset, until the twilight glow disappears. Isha: from then until half the night.
learn.title: Asr, Maghrib and Isha

learn.en: Each prayer must be offered in its time. Use a prayer timetable, or ask Mum and Dad.
learn.title: On time

learn.en: Rak'ahs: Fajr 2, Dhuhr 4, Asr 4, Maghrib 3, Isha 4.
learn.title: How many rak'ahs?

learn.en: A rak'ah: Al-Fatihah standing, another surah (in the first two), ruku', standing up, two sujud with sitting in between.
learn.title: What is a rak'ah?

learn.en: “Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times.” (Qur'an 4:103)
learn.title: From the Qur'an

quiz.en: The time of Fajr lasts until…

think.q: Can you find today's prayer times on a timetable or app with Mum or Dad?
think.a: Write them down and tick each prayer when you pray it on time!

parents.summary: Each prayer has its time; rak'ahs: Fajr 2, Dhuhr 4, Asr 4, Maghrib 3, Isha 4; a rak'ah = standing, ruku', sujud.
parents.tip: Make a prayer chart for the fridge with the times and rak'ahs.
